lines.text: Hackers hid a card-stealing script on five online stores just before Black Friday.
The script got in through a marketing tracker, a cookie-banner setting, or a file on a store's own network.
lines.title: Getting in

lines.text: It used WebRTC, the browser feature behind video calls. Security tools often watch it less closely.
lines.title: The sneaky channel

lines.text: At phone checkout, the script loaded itself, copied the card details, and sent them out the same hidden way.
lines.title: What it did

lines.text: It ran only on phone-sized screens, so desktop checks would miss it. All five stores removed it on 24 or 25 November.
lines.title: Where it hid

lines.text: Site owners can set a rule listing only the hosts a payment page may contact. That blocks the script from arriving.
lines.title: The fix

lines.text: The takeaway: keep third-party scripts off payment pages, and check your card statements.
lines.title: Takeaways
